slides.title:
He lost his first store
over a *lease*. Then he
built Walmart.
slides.sub: The Sam Walton story, in 9 slides 👇

slides.title:
Sam Walton, 27, buys a
*Ben Franklin* variety store
in Newport, Arkansas 🏪
slides.sub:
$5,000 of his own savings.
$20,000 borrowed from his father-in-law
(Entrepreneur).

slides.title:
Across the street: a rival.
Sam is *always over there*
checking prices 👀
slides.sub:
Sales: $80,000 → $225,000 in 3 years.
"Always over there checking on John"
— his wife Helen (Business Insider).

slides.title:
His lease has *no renewal
option*. The landlord
takes the store 😶
slides.sub:
He gives it to his own son
(Encyclopedia of Arkansas).
Sam has to start over, somewhere else.

slides.title:
He rides a bus all night
to *copy* two self-service
stores in Minnesota 🚌
slides.sub:
"I liked it. So I did that too."
His new store is one of the first
self-service variety stores in the US.

slides.title:
Ben Franklin says *no* to
his discount idea. He opens
the first Walmart anyway 🛒
slides.sub:
He borrows heavily to do it,
in Rogers, Arkansas (Entrepreneur,
Encyclopedia of Arkansas).

slides.title: Most everything I've done I've *copied* from someone else.
slides.author:
Sam Walton,
Made in America (1992)

slides.title:
stores in 19 countries.
*$713B* in revenue 📈
slides.sub:
Fiscal year to Jan. 31, 2026, +4.7%.
E-commerce alone: $150.4B
(Walmart via Retail Insight Network).

slides.title:
Study the best
stores. Then do
*what works*. 👀
slides.sub:
✅ Visit your top 3 competitors' sites
✅ Note what makes buying easy
✅ Copy the idea, not the design
